name: Nawaf Salam
role: Prime Minister of Lebanon (President of the Council of Ministers, رئيس مجلس الوزراء)
bio: Nawaf Salam, born in Beirut in 1953 into a prominent Sunni Muslim family (his uncle Saeb Salam and his cousin Tammam Salam were prime ministers), is a jurist, diplomat and academic who has been Prime Minister of Lebanon since 8 February 2025. He taught at the Sorbonne and the American University of Beirut, was Lebanon's ambassador to the United Nations from 2007 to 2017, and sat on the International Court of Justice from 2018, presiding over it from February 2024, including in South Africa's genocide case against Israel (which Israel rejects) and in the July 2024 advisory opinion on Israel's policies in the Palestinian territories; he resigned from the Court on 14 January 2025 after 84 of the 128 MPs named him Prime Minister, with Hezbollah and Amal naming no one. Without party affiliation, he formed a 24-minister cabinet under President Joseph Aoun whose ministerial statement, for the first time in two decades, left out any reference to 'resistance' and committed the state to a monopoly on weapons. In August 2025 his government tasked the army with bringing all weapons under state control, which Hezbollah rejected; when Hezbollah fired on Israel on 2 March 2026 after the US–Israeli strikes on Iran, the cabinet banned the group's military and security activities, and the war that followed, in which more than 4,300 people were killed in Lebanon according to Lebanese authorities, led to direct negotiations with Israel in Washington and a US-brokered framework agreement signed on 26 June 2026, whose implementation was stalled as of October 2026. His government obtained laws on banking secrecy (April 2025), bank resolution (July 2025, amended in September 2026) and judicial independence (2025), and sent a 'financial gap' bill on depositors' losses to parliament in December 2025, but had no new IMF staff-level agreement as of October 2026; the parliamentary election due in May 2026 did not take place, parliament having extended its own term to May 2028.
